# Building with occam while the person watches

`occam run --help` is the guide to writing requests, and each command's `--help` says what it takes. This skill says
what the guide does not: how to work with a person who watches the model in occam's viewer and selects in it.

## Run occam alone, and write requests with your file tool

A project may let only `occam` commands run in the shell. So run each `occam` command on its own, with no `&&`, pipe
or redirection, and write each request file with your file-writing tool (Write), never with `cat`, `echo` or a heredoc.
`occam run` takes the request as a file, not inline. If a shell command is refused, that says nothing about `occam`:
run the `occam` command alone.

## Start the viewer, and say where to look

Choose the model's file, here `part.occam`, and start its viewer before the first run:

```sh
occam view --model part.occam
```

It opens the page in a browser, prints the page's address and returns: tell the person to look there. Until a run
writes the model it also says there is no model at `part.occam`, which is expected. The viewer keeps running between
commands, and `occam view` again starts nothing new and prints the same address.

## Build in runs you can check

The page redraws after each run that changes the model, so build in steps the person can follow, and read each result
before the next. Write a request with your file tool, here `block.json`:

```json
{"schema": 1, "units": {"length": "mm", "angle": "deg"}, "steps": [
  {"op": "face", "label": "outline", "outer": {"points": [[0, 0, 0], [40, 0, 0], [40, 30, 0], [0, 30, 0]], "closed": true}},
  {"op": "extrude", "label": "block", "face": "outline", "vector": [0, 0, 10]}
]}
```

Then run it, naming the file:

```sh
occam run --model part.occam block.json
```

The result names what each step made, such as `body:0/2`. A label names only what its own request made: a later
request names it by its id.

## Read the selection when the person says "the selected"

In the page a click selects a face or an edge, and shift-click adds or removes one. When the person speaks of the
selected face, the one they clicked, or "this", read what they selected:

```sh
occam selection --model part.occam
```

It describes each selected id as `occam describe` does. A flat face gives its plane's `origin` and `normal`, and its
box as `low` and `high`. The centre of a flat face square to the axes is the middle of `low` and `high`, not its
`origin`. Its `normal` may point into the solid: the outside is the side the body's bounds do not reach. If nothing is
selected, ask the person to click what they mean; if the selection is refused as `view.selection-stale`, ask them to
select again.

## Highlight before you change what is selected

Show the person what you are about to act on, by its id, before the run that acts on it:

```sh
occam highlight --model part.occam face:5/1
```

The page draws it in a colour of its own until the next run that changes the model. Here the selected face is the
block's top, `face:5/1`, from `low` about (0, 0, 10) to `high` about (40, 30, 10), so its centre is (20, 15, 10). A pin
of radius 3 and height 8 stands on it with its frame's origin there and its `z` pointing out of the block. Write
`pin.json` with your file tool:

```json
{"schema": 1, "units": {"length": "mm", "angle": "deg"}, "steps": [
  {"op": "cylinder", "label": "pin", "radius": 3, "height": 8, "frame": {"origin": [20, 15, 10], "z": [0, 0, 1]}}
]}
```

```sh
occam run --model part.occam pin.json
```

This build has no boolean, fillet or chamfer, so a body placed on a face stays a body of its own: say so if the person
asks to join, cut or round.

## Measure to confirm

Check what a run made against what was asked before you say it is done. A request of measures alone leaves the model as
it was. Write `check.json` with your file tool:

```json
{"schema": 1, "units": {"length": "mm", "angle": "deg"}, "steps": [
  {"op": "measure", "target": "body:1/1", "what": ["volume", "bounds"]}
]}
```

```sh
occam run --model part.occam check.json
```

## Stop the viewer when the person is done

Leave the viewer running between requests. When the person says they are done, stop it:

```sh
occam view --model part.occam --stop
```
I'll check the request format first, since this build has no boolean operations and the hole needs to be built into the profile.

content.content:
Run a request on a model, and write the model back if the whole request went through.

--help shows how to write a request.

Usage: occam run [OPTIONS] --model <FILE> <REQUEST>

Arguments:
  <REQUEST>
          The request: a JSON file of steps

Options:
      --json
          Give the result, or the reports refusing it, in one JSON form on standard output

      --model <FILE>
          The model: read if it exists and made new if not, and written back only if the whole request goes through

      --binary
          Write the model as the binary twin. Otherwise a model keeps its encoding, and a new one is readable JSON

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

A request is a JSON file of steps, run in order on the model:

  {"schema": 1, "units": {"length": "mm", "angle": "deg"}, "steps": [
    {"op": "box", "label": "block", "size": [40, 20, 10]},
    {"op": "measure", "target": "block", "what": ["volume"]}
  ]}

  schema     1
  units      length: mm, cm, m or in; angle: rad or deg. Every number the request gives is in these.
  tolerance  {"length": number, "angle": number}, optional: what a new model is built to (1e-7 mm and 1e-9 rad if left out).
  steps      each with "op", an optional "label", and its operation's fields, below. A field that names an entity takes
             an earlier step's label, for what that step made, or an id such as body:0/1.

A point or a vector is [x, y, z]; a direction is [x, y, z] of any length. A frame is {"origin": point, "z": direction,
"x": direction}, each optional, and the world's if left out.

A face's outer wire and its holes may be written in place, as a wire step's fields, instead of naming wire steps. Here a
plate with a round hole is extruded, and a profile drawn in the xz plane is revolved whole about an axis in it:

  {"schema": 1, "units": {"length": "mm", "angle": "deg"}, "steps": [
    {"op": "face", "label": "plate",
     "outer": {"points": [[0, 0, 0], [60, 0, 0], [60, 40, 0], [0, 40, 0]], "closed": true},
     "holes": [{"edges": [{"circle": {"centre": [30, 20, 0], "radius": 5, "normal": [0, 0, 1]}}]}]},
    {"op": "extrude", "face": "plate", "vector": [0, 0, 6]},
    {"op": "face", "label": "profile",
     "outer": {"points": [[100, 0, 0], [120, 0, 0], [120, 0, 30], [100, 0, 30]], "closed": true}},
    {"op": "revolve", "profile": "profile", "origin": [100, 0, 0], "axis": [0, 0, 1], "angle": 360}
  ]}

Operations:
  box        size [x, y, z]; frame
  cylinder   radius; height, along the frame's z; frame
  sphere     radius; frame
  cone       radius1 at the base and radius2 at the top, either but not both 0; height; frame
  torus      major, the radius its tube's centre runs round; minor, the tube's, less than major; frame
  wedge      size [x, y, z]; top {"start": where it begins along x, "width": along x}; frame
  wire       points [point, ...], with straight edges between, or edges [{"line": [from, to]} or {"arc": [from, through, to]} or {"circle": {"centre": point, "radius": length, "normal": direction}}, ...]; and closed: true to join the last to the first by a straight edge, if they do not meet
  face       outer, a closed planar wire, and holes [wire, ...] inside it, if any; a wire is a label, an id or a wire written in place
  extrude    face, a planar face; vector [x, y, z], the way and length it is swept
  revolve    profile, a face or a wire; origin, a point on the axis; axis, a direction; angle
  transform  target, a body; scale, a number or three along about's axes, if any; about, a frame; frame, where the world's frame goes, after the scale. The body keeps its ids
  copy       target, scale, about and frame, as for transform; the copy has new ids
  measure    target, an entity; what [measurement, ...], or all the target has if left out

Measurements: volume, area, centre-of-mass, bounds.
Refused by this build, by name: boolean, fillet, chamfer.

Bad input is refused before any step runs, each with its code and its place, such as steps[2].size[0]. A step that
fails stops the request, and the model is written back only if every step went through. The result says what each
step made, created, changed and deleted, by id, and describes what it created. A description says which step made
an entity as this numbers a request's steps, from 0, with the step's operation, even in a later command; a copy's
also names the body it copied.

The plate is in `part.occam` and matches the spec. It is 80 × 60 × 10 mm, lying flat on the xy plane with its bottom at z = 0, and has a 12 mm hole centred at (20, 30).

The measured volume is 46,869.03 mm³. That is 48,000 mm³ for the solid block less π × 6² × 10 ≈ 1,131 mm³ for the hole, so the hole is through the full thickness. The bounds run from (0, 0, 0) to (80, 60, 10).

I built the hole into the face's outline, so the model has no boolean step. The model is one body, `body:0/2`.

The viewer is still running at http://127.0.0.1:46247/e48c1d44ea314911da16aa63b9195e07/ in case you want to look. I can stop it with `occam view --model part.occam --stop` when you're done.
